p0.original: 第十四章 从应激到健康和幸福
p0.en: Chapter XIV. From stress to health and happiness.

p1.en: Translator of this chapter: Liu Chau

p3.original: 本章视频导读，请扫描二维码观看。
p3.en: Scan the QR code to watch the video introduction to this chapter.

p4.original: 应激与我们的生活息息相关。当谈及应激的时候，我们似乎都选择避而远之，因为它让我们产生不愉快的感受，有时还让我们感到痛苦、不安。然而，应激又是无处不在的，当个体处在一定的人际关系与社会环境中时，应激便如影随形。同时，应激对我们的身心健康与幸福感也会产生深远的影响。如何与应激相处无疑是人生中一个重要的课题。
p4.en: It's all about our lives. When it comes to stress, it seems that we all choose to stay away, because it gives us unpleasant feelings and sometimes pains and worries. However, stress is pervasive, and it is always present when an individual is in a certain interpersonal relationship and social environment. At the same time, stress has far-reaching implications for our physical and mental health and well-being. How to live with stress is undoubtedly an important topic in life.

p5.original: 那究竟什么会导致应激呢？我们知道，当经历重大的生活变故、自然或人为灾难等创伤性事件时，会不可避免地伴随着极度应激。然而，有意思的是，应激的来源并非全都是消极事件，也包括一些积极事件。通过本章的学习我们会知道，任何变化都会带来潜在影响，并要求我们做出改变以适应新的环境，这就是应激的来源。
p5.en: So what exactly causes the stress? We know that extreme stress is inevitably accompanied by traumatic events, such as major life changes, natural or man-made disasters. It is interesting, however, that the sources of stress are not all negative and include some positive events. Learning through this chapter will show that any change has potential implications and will require us to adapt to the new environment, which is the source of stress.

p6.original: 生活中充满了大大小小的应激源，那么，应激对我们的影响全都是负面的吗？我们常说，适当的应激也是动力，确实如此，有时我们需要应激，某些应激有助于我们鞭策和完善自己，促进我们的成长。通过本章的学习，我们可以得知，适当的应激引起的情绪唤醒有利于我们集中注意力，帮助我们做好准备。此外，或许你不知道的是，有时我们也需要应激带来的糟糕感受。例如，当你在人际关系中遭受他人的拒绝或排斥时，或许会感到沮丧与难过，然而正是这种沮丧可以阻止你建立不明智的人际关系，保护你免受进一步的伤害。
p6.en: Life is full of big and small sources of stress, so is the impact of stress all negative? We have often said that the right stress is also the driving force, indeed, and sometimes we need it, and that some stress helps us to spur and perfect ourselves and to promote our growth. Through the study of this chapter, we can learn that the emotional awakening caused by appropriate stress helps to focus our attention and help us prepare. Moreover, perhaps you do not know that sometimes we also need the bad feeling of stress. For example, when you are rejected or excluded from human relations, you may feel frustration and distress, but it is precisely that frustration that prevents you from building unwise interpersonal relations and protecting you from further harm.

p7.original: 而在感知应激和应对应激的过程中，不同个体也存在差异，一部分是由于人格特征的差异造成的。例如，面对相同的挫折，对于乐观坚韧的人来说，问题似乎总能迎刃而解。此外，认知评估也起着重要作用。这需要你有意识地站在积极的角度看待应激事件，认识到是对事件的看法而不是事件本身引发了你的情绪和感受。认知评估不仅仅存在于应对应激的过程中，它甚至是所有应激事件引发的情绪和感受中一个非常关键的心理因素。
p7.en: There are also differences between individuals in the process of sensory and coping with stress, partly due to differences in personality characteristics. For example, in the face of the same setbacks, the problem seems always to be solved for those who are optimistic and resilient. In addition, cognitive assessment plays an important role. This requires you to consciously take a positive view of the stress, recognizing that it is the perception of the incident, rather than the event itself, that triggers your emotions and feelings. Cognitive assessment is not only a critical psychological factor in coping with stress, but even in the emotions and feelings generated by all stress events.

p8.original: 当然，你心中肯定还有很多对应激的好奇与疑问。而本章的学习将为你开启一段探秘应激的旅程，随着对应激的深入探索，这些疑问的答案将一一得到揭晓，我们将获悉认知因素在应激感知中的作用，了解身体在应对应激时会产生战斗或逃跑反应，收获聚焦问题和聚焦情绪的应对应激的两大法宝等。
p8.en: Of course, you must have a lot of resonant curiosity and doubt. And learning this chapter will open up a journey to explore stress, and, as the counter-heavy is explored in depth, the answers to those questions will be revealed. We will learn about the role of cognitive factors in stressors, about how bodies respond to stress in combat or escape, and about the two great powers of focus and emotional stress.

p9.original: 在这趟丰富且有趣的旅程中，愿你能更好地理解应激，找到自己与应激共处的方式。
p9.en: On this rich and interesting journey, may you better understand stress and find your own way of living with stress.
